## Preparation

You need:

- R
- RStudio
- Git, which you can check with `git --version` in the terminal
- A GitHub account

It is recommended to connect RStudio to GitHub using an SSH key. Never use your GitHub password directly as an authentication method.

## Find the GitHub repository link

1. Go to the GitHub repository page.
2. Click the green **`<> Code`** button.
3. Choose the **SSH** or **HTTPS** tab, then copy the link.

Examples:

- SSH: `git@github.com:UserName/project-name.git`
- HTTPS: `https://github.com/UserName/project-name.git`

## Clone in RStudio

1. Open **RStudio**.
2. Go to **File > New Project**.
3. Choose **Version Control**.
4. Select **Git**.
5. Paste the link into the **Repository URL** field.
6. Choose a local folder for the project.
7. Click **Create Project**.

You can now start working in your new RStudio project.

## GitHub authentication error

If you get an error such as:

```text
fatal: Authentication failed
remote: Support for password authentication was removed...
```

This usually means that HTTPS was used without a personal access token or another valid authentication setup.

Two solutions are possible:

- Generate a **personal access token** (PAT) on GitHub and use it as the password.
- Configure **SSH**, which is simpler and more robust in the long run.

## Configure SSH with GitHub

```bash
# 1. Generate an SSH key if needed
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your-email@example.com"

# 2. Add the SSH key to the agent
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

# 3. Copy the public key
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```

Then paste this key into **GitHub > Settings > SSH and GPG keys > New SSH key**.

Documentation: <https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh>
